title: Internal temperature too high
shortDescription: Generator overheated; cooktop in protection mode.
fullDescription: Thermador induction cooktops display E001 when the IGBT generator under the glass exceeds safe temperature. Most often caused by inadequate ventilation or blocked cooling intake under the cabinet.

fixSteps.title: Verify cabinet cutout
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm install meets Thermador airflow spec.

whenToCallPro: If E001 returns with proper ventilation.

faq.a: Wait for full cool-down before retrying.

title: Cooling fan failure
shortDescription: Cooling fan not at expected RPM.
fullDescription: E002 is shown when the cooling fan tachometer reads below threshold. Replace fan or clear obstruction.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum fan
fixSteps.instruction: Lift cooktop, vacuum dust from fan.

faq.a: Annually if pulled for service.

title: Pan recognition failure
shortDescription: Cookware not detected on selected zone.
fullDescription: E005 is shown when the active zone cannot detect a magnetic pan. Use induction-compatible cookware sized to the zone.

fixSteps.title: Magnet test
fixSteps.instruction: Verify pan base attracts a magnet strongly.

faq.a: Induction needs ferromagnetic base.

title: Touch control stuck
fullDescription: E011 means a touch button reads pressed for more than 30 seconds. Clean the panel - spills, water droplets, and pan handles often trigger this.

faq.a: Activate child lock when cleaning.

title: Generator communication error
shortDescription: Lost link between UI and induction generator.
fullDescription: E021 indicates a communication fault between the user interface and the induction power module. Reseating internal harnesses or replacing the module is required.

faq.a: No, presets are in main control.

title: Sensor open
fullDescription: E031 indicates a coil thermistor failed open. The affected element is locked out for safety.

faq.a: Yes, until repaired.

title: Sensor shorted
fullDescription: E032 reports a shorted coil thermistor. Replace the sensor.

faq.a: Yes, same thermistor.

title: Mains voltage out of range
shortDescription: Supply voltage too high or low.
fullDescription: E042 alerts that supply voltage drifted outside the 200-250 V window. Verify breaker and circuit health.

faq.a: Whole-house surge protector recommended.

title: Memory checksum error
fullDescription: E051 indicates the EEPROM checksum failed. Power cycle; if the code persists, the control needs replacement.

faq.a: Possible - install whole-house protection.

title: Touch keypad fault
fullDescription: ER22 occurs when the capacitive touch electrodes return invalid readings. Cleaning often clears it; persistent ER22 means the user interface needs replacement.
whenToCallPro: If reset fails, UI replacement needed.

faq.a: E011 is single key stuck; ER22 is full panel failure.

title: Generator IGBT Overheat
shortDescription: The induction generator IGBT module exceeded its temperature limit.
fullDescription: Thermador induction cooktop error E003 indicates IGBT overheat. The affected zone (or all zones) is disabled until the fault is cleared. Most E003 faults require a Thermador-authorized service call due to high-voltage induction electronics.

causes.cause: Wiring harness loose at generator board

symptoms: E003 flashing on the touch display
Audible beeping until fault is acknowledged

fixSteps.title: Power cycle at the breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the cooktop's dedicated breaker for 5 minutes, then restore power and check whether the code returns at startup.

fixSteps.title: Verify ventilation
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm that the under-counter ventilation cutout meets Thermador spec - induction generators overheat in restricted spaces.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Most Thermador induction faults require an authorized technician with the diagnostic interface to test coils and the IGBT module.

whenToCallPro: Induction cooktops carry high voltage even when off due to large capacitors. Always use Thermador-authorized service for E003.

title: Pan Detection Sensor Drift
shortDescription: Induction pan detection sensor reads out of range.
fullDescription: E091 fires when one of the induction zone pan-detection coils returns a value outside calibration limits, preventing pan recognition.

causes.cause: Foil or magnet residue on glass

fixSteps.title: Clean glass
fixSteps.instruction: Remove all metallic residue from the cooktop surface.

whenToCallPro: Sensor replacement requires accessing the cooktop from below the counter — call Thermador service.

faq.a: Magnetic ferrous pans are required; aluminum/glass will not heat on induction.

title: Touchscreen Calibration Drift
fullDescription: E101 logs when capacitive surface detects multiple ghost taps over a short interval.

fixSteps.title: Clean glass
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the cooktop with isopropyl alcohol and let dry.

whenToCallPro: Replace touch glass if ghost taps persist after cleaning.

faq.q: Will the cooktop turn on by itself?
faq.a: No — child-lock prevents that, and ghost taps still require pattern matching.

title: Inverter Module Over-Temp
shortDescription: One of the four induction inverters exceeded thermal limit.
fullDescription: E111 trips when a power module reaches 95°C and shuts down the affected zone to protect electronics.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the cooktop's lower air intake (under cabinet) is unobstructed.

whenToCallPro: If vents are clear and fan runs, the inverter module needs Thermador service.

faq.a: Yes — only the affected zone is offline.

title: Bridge Function Sensor Mismatch
shortDescription: Bridge function detected mismatched coil temperatures.
fullDescription: E121 fires when the two zones bridged together report widely different coil temperatures.

causes.cause: Pan does not span both zones evenly

fixSteps.title: Reposition pan
fixSteps.instruction: Center pan across both bridged zones.

whenToCallPro: If repositioning fails, sensor replacement needed.

faq.q: What if my pan is small?
faq.a: Use a single zone; bridge requires a long pan or griddle.

title: Power-Sharing Limit Exceeded
shortDescription: Cooktop reduced power on a zone due to total wattage limit.
fullDescription: E131 is a soft alert that the cooktop's power-sharing logic engaged because all zones were running at max.

causes.cause: All four zones at max simultaneously

fixSteps.title: Stagger zones
fixSteps.instruction: Reduce one zone's power level to release shared headroom.

whenToCallPro: If the alert appears at low total load, an installer must verify the power configuration.

faq.a: No — all induction cooktops share power across zones.

title: Glass Surface Temperature High
shortDescription: Glass thermistor exceeded safe surface temperature.
fullDescription: E141 trips when the surface thermistor detects temperatures above 600°C, often after a dry pan was left on a zone.

fixSteps.title: Remove pan
fixSteps.instruction: Lift the empty pan off and let the surface cool fully.

whenToCallPro: If the cooktop was used normally, the thermistor may be drifted and need replacement.

faq.a: Glass is rated for these temperatures, but inspect for cracks before resuming.

title: Home Connect Pairing Lost
fullDescription: E151 logs once when the connectivity module loses its stored Wi-Fi credentials.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair
fixSteps.instruction: Re-run the Home Connect pairing flow in the app.

whenToCallPro: Replace module only after multiple pairing failures.

faq.a: Optional — provides remote monitoring and recipe download.

title: Hot Surface Indicator LED Failure
fullDescription: E161 trips when the residual-heat indicator LED does not respond to its self-test pulse on power-up.
symptoms: Residual heat icon does not show

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Pull cooktop and reseat indicator harness from below cabinet.

whenToCallPro: Replace LED board if reseating fails.

faq.a: Yes, somewhat — without the residual-heat warning, accidental burns are easier.

title: Quick Boost Timeout
shortDescription: Quick boost mode disengaged after maximum time.

faq.a: Boost cycles use bridged inverters; the limit prevents prolonged thermal stress.
